extracted.intended_audience: administrative analysts, management planners, and government agency administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for administrative analysts and management planning units on organization design, procedure manual construction, authority delegation, and work distribution within government agencies and large organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst duty to minimize interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange ways and means for the line executives to initiate, supervise, and control operations with the minimum amount of interference to direct activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative analyst should design procedures that enable line executives to perform their functions with minimal external intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous observation and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly observe the operation of the administrative machine and apply analysis by function, by units of organization, and by administrative sequence to the facts and situations found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study relation of administration to operation, keep the administrator informed on adaptation to changing objectives/conditions/functions/techniques, and prepare data for planning necessary changes so rearrangements may be made with the least confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribute to administrative flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative analyst relieves line officials of the extra burden of preparing organizational changes and new procedures, contributing to administrative flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By preparing organization changes and procedures, the analyst enables quicker, less disruptive adaptation to change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management planning unit core responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the effectiveness of the basic plan of organization and develop improved plans to facilitate accomplishment of agency objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes proper division and functional distribution of work, establishment of a sound structure of authority and control, provision of appropriate staff facilities and services, elimination of jurisdictional conflicts, and proper program coordination to enable the chief administrator to energize and coordinate subdivisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive mandate for planning units
rubrics_metrics.description: The management planning unit should be authorized and required to play a major part in the planning and periodic revision of the organization structure and assignment of functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should not sit on the sidelines until a line executive requests services; it should supply analytical and technical data and attend to the mechanical details of reorganization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized clearing-house for standardized procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Management planning units commonly act as clearing-houses for standardized written procedure such as rules, regulations, instructions, and flow charts, and may approve printed and duplicated forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions may include mapping recurrent sequences, routing non-recurrent sequences, timing, scheduling, and controlling flow of work to ensure organization, distribution of functions, and procedures are harmonious and unit sizes adjusted to workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidated subject-matter procedure manuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend toward the establishment of consolidated manuals and digests arranged by subject matter to bring together relevant laws, decisions, rules, policies, assignments of function, and specific instructions in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective is to enable the user to find all needed information on any one subject in one place; particularly valuable in government where legal and fiscal requirements are numerous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange manuals by major function with cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Current tendency is to arrange manuals by major functions, breaking down by sub-functions and sequences; when sequences cover more than one function treat them under the dominant function with cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No single 'best way' exists — manuals must be assembled to fit each organization's functions; use dominant-function criterion when classification dilemmas arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify subjects by dominant function
rubrics_metrics.description: Material is classified according to whichever function is dominant in the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group activities for which line units are mainly responsible under line functions and those staff units perform or supervise under staff functions; refine boundaries and assignments where overlap ('no man's land').

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuals reflect organizational clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual is a compilation of the organization's standing administrative determinations and necessarily reflects the clarity or confusion of overall procedural management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear manual requires refined, clarified assignments of functions and zones of competence; a disorganized manual indicates procedural management issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate analyst output with line administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Results of procedural surveys should be reviewed by line officials, and plans/instructions formulated by analysts should be issued by the administrators responsible for the policies/programs concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where material relates exclusively to techniques of administrative management (e.g., flow charts, scheduling methods), the chief administrative analyst may promulgate it under his signature; otherwise, routing through appropriate administrators preserves coordination and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature authority distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural documents that regulate activities of all personnel or more than one division should carry the signature of the highest administrator, but many documents should be signed by the head of the relevant division or staff officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve administrator signature for matters crossing divisional lines; allow division heads to sign within their jurisdiction to preserve delegated responsibilities and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary concentration of approval authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring administrator or board approval for all material included in a procedure manual is unnecessary and undesirable as it reclaims delegated responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer universal classification of material with division heads signing instructions within their jurisdictions, reserving highest-level sign-off to cross-divisional issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst-line cooperative development of procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Shaping procedures should be a co-operative undertaking where the analyst pools administrative knowledge with the technical skill of the line officer; the line officer states objectives and basic operations while the analyst arranges and specifies tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agreement is impossible, refer to the superior; present facts objectively and conflicting recommendations separately to avoid perceptions of 'putting things over.' Avoid special pleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of administrative analysts for impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure impartiality, the administrative analyst should be placed directly subordinate to the responsible administrator or in a division concerned with management problems rather than detailed staff operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid locating analysts in personnel or legal offices where specialized outlooks may bias their work; budget office placement may bias if the branch seeks monetary savings without regard to consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-level management planning units
rubrics_metrics.description: In large and complex organizations, management planning units at various levels (central and bureau) may be desirable with central units providing technical supervision and assistance to bureau units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central unit reports to top officials (Secretary/Executive Officer) and deals with departmental organization and procedure; bureau units report to bureau chiefs and handle local issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize co-operation, coordination, and facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts should co-operate with each other and operating officials, strive to make administrative processes as simple and economical as possible, and avoid perfectionism that interferes with program accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The emphasis should be on coordination and facilitation above technical perfection for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of a management planning office (Civil Aeronautics example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide over-all management planning and advisory services including advising staff/operating officers on planning/operations/management controls; conducting surveys/analyses of organization, functions, staffing, performance; developing reports/controls for evaluation; controlling issuance of directives; assisting in major installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete list (Figure 14-A) serves as a model for the kinds of duties a management planning office should perform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of plan must reconcile function, unit, sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of plan requires bringing ways and means into exact quantitative, qualitative, and functional relationships; decide when each task shall be done, by whom, and where the doers shall be placed in the organization structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must reconcile function, unit of organization, and administrative sequence; weigh capacity of concentration points and processing units and weave interlocking channels to prevent conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimit fields of work precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: First step in shaping work programs is a precise delimitation of fields of work; define spheres of work for each division in terms of subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In non-routine administration plan from function and project rather than sequence; let flow of sequences evolve from natural order and content of tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign standing work by content of tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Standing work-assignments should be made in terms of the content of tasks rather than the tasks themselves so that new tasks have predetermined assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marking out areas of operation should be joint between administrators and analysts; analyst provides charts and descriptions, administrator retains primary responsibility for major divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous survey and reorganization
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning of fields of work and organization units is an ongoing process requiring continuous survey and analysis based on first-hand inspection and fact-gathering; use conclusions for re-defining and re-organizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations that never change are likely stagnant; make periodic, data-based adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work distribution within units: balanced workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Within reasonable-size units, assign tasks according to character, difficulty, and relation to other tasks with the objective of giving each individual a balanced workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use methods from 'Analysis by Units of Organization' and the criteria for evaluating administrative sequences: (1) each task should contribute positively to the basic purpose; (2) similar tasks should be combined; (3) administrative moves should be as few and short as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measureable work units and objective equalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for measurable elements in tasks and apply work units (common denominators like work-hour) so work loads can be equalized on objective bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standard units for common operations (transcribing, typing, filing). Develop units for specialized operations by observation; for highly variable tasks derive units from periodic work-record analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between direct channels and specialist use
rubrics_metrics.description: When distributing work between units strike a balance between seeking the most direct channels (fewest moves) and using specialist skill and experience effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If many divergent technical phases exist, compromise so the product is sound without overly complicated procedure; place specialists so recurrent projects remain within major divisions where practical.
